title: Phenomena seen in discrete simple programs also occur in simple continuous systems

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Phenomena seen in discrete simple programs also occur in simple continuous systems

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Essentially all of the phenomena observed in discrete simple programs can also be found in continuous systems with fairly simple rules.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I suspect that essentially all of the various phenomena that we have observed in discrete systems in the past several chapters can in fact also be found even in continuous systems with fairly simple rules.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 4, “Systems Based on Numbers”; section “Continuous Versus Discrete Systems” (from p. 167), p. 168. Scope: continuous systems such as continuous cellular automata, iterated maps and partial differential equations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch04-27: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Many proposed correspondences can be sought and reproduced with existing solvers and catalogs. The nearly universal scope and open-ended phenomenon class cannot be exhausted, making only finite subsets resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: List a finite preregistered taxonomy of discrete phenomena, then search specified low-complexity continuous models for robust instances under numerical refinement. Missing phenomena after systematic searches weaken the finite taxonomy claim, while examples confirm individual correspondences.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A complete taxonomy of discrete phenomena is unavailable.

Failure to find a continuous analogue does not prove absence.

Essentially all and fairly simple are undefined.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.4

discriminating power: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Some of the discrete phenomena, including irregular evolution and localized structures, already have continuous examples that can be resimulated. 'Essentially all' of the phenomena from the preceding chapters is an open-ended list, and absence of an example is weak evidence against a suspicion that an example exists. The claim is therefore testable piece by piece and not as a finished universal statement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: List the phenomena already recorded for discrete simple programs, such as repetition, nesting, apparent randomness, and localized structures, and search simple continuous cellular automata, maps, and partial differential equations for each one. A continuous example supports that item; a proved obstruction for one item would refute 'essentially all,' while a failed search would not.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Numerical artifacts can imitate localized structures and nesting in continuum simulations.

Failure to find a continuous example does not refute an existence claim, so the universal statement is hard to falsify.
